title: Micro-interaction grammar for rollout recovery flows
creator: Maya Flynn
description:
Objective: Establish a consistent micro-interaction grammar for 'rollout recovery' states across the Redwood Console. These are the transient, edge, and error states users encounter when a rollout partially fails, stalls, or is automatically rolled back. The goal is to reduce cognitive load, make remediation paths discoverable, and ensure interactions are accessible and performant.

Scope:
- Define patterns for inline status badges, transient toasts, and expanded detail panels when a rollout enters a recovery path.
- Create animation/transition guidelines (duration, easing, entrance/exit) that respect prefers-reduced-motion.
- Specify affordances for quick remediation (retry, pause, pin logs, escalate) including primary/secondary action placement and confirmation patterns.
- Define keyboard and screen-reader states for each interaction (focus order, aria-live regions, announcements).
- Produce Figma components (tokens + interactive variants) and a dev-ready handoff doc with code-ready motion specs.

Deliverables:
- High-fidelity Figma file with interactive prototypes for three canonical recovery scenarios: (1) partial instance failure with auto-retry, (2) long-running stalled rollout with manual resume, (3) automatic rollback with investigation affordances.
- Component spec sheet (timing, easing, visual states, accessibility notes).
- Handoff doc: copy guidance, QA checklist, list of telemetry events to track (for UX success).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Design system components exist for badges/toasts/expansion panels and include motion specs and accessibility annotations.
2) Prototypes demonstrate clear remediation flows with < 3 clicks from detection to action.
3) PM/Eng sign-off on action placement and telemetry events.
4) QA checklist covers keyboard flows, screen-reader announcements, motion preferences, and edge-case timings.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- We must balance visible feedback with not adding noise to the console; toasts should not obscure critical controls.
- Telemetry calls for fine-grained interaction tracking may increase cost; recommend sampling for low-severity flows.
- For legacy browsers we fallback to instantaneous state changes (no animation).

Notes for devs: include request for precise CSS variables and a short JSON snippet of motion tokens (duration,easing) to be agreed during handoff.

2026-03-03 - Arjun Patel: Confirmed feasibility of inline log pinning; engineering prefers a non-blocking optimistic UI for retry actions. Mentioned existing toast component will need a 'persistent' variant for recovery notifications.

2026-03-05 - Maya Flynn: Uploaded low-fidelity explorations (links in attachments). Feedback from Jenna Morales (PM): prefer 'resume' as primary in stalled flows; avoid destructive language in toasts. Action: Update copy and create resume-first prototype.

2026-03-07 - Design review with stakeholders (Jenna Morales, Priya Rao - Security, Lars Håkansson - SRE): Priya requested explicit mention of audit log entries when users manually trigger retries; Lars requested a backoff visualization for auto-retry attempts. Action: Add telemetry event names and visual backoff hint to detail panel.

2026-03-08 - Accessibility review (internal): Noted that aria-live regions should announce numeric progress changes only when focus is outside the panel to avoid verbosity. Also recommended 200ms minimum reduced-motion fallback. Action: Update spec.

2026-03-09 - Visual polish pass: tightened timing to 160ms for fades, adjusted scale from 1.04 to 1.02 for subtle emphasis, updated color token for 'recovering' badge to ensure 4.5:1 contrast on light mode. Added examples for dark mode.

2026-03-10 - Arjun Patel: Engineering review completed. Confirmed component variants and motion tokens plausible. Raised one implementation question about stacking toasts when multiple rollouts recover simultaneously. Proposed approach documented in PR. Requesting final design sign-off by 2026-03-12.
